title: Sheinbaum Presents Draft Decree to Force Digital Platforms to Take Down Content That Incites Violence and Hate
author: Alonso Urrutia and Arturo Sánchez
content:
_This article by[Alonso Urrutia and Arturo
Sánchez](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Alonso%20Urrutia%20y%20Arturo%20S%C3%A1nchez)
originally appeared in the [October 9, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/10/09/politica/sheinbaum-
presenta-proyecto-de-decreto-para-prohibir-contenidos-violentos-en-
plataformas-digitales), Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City**. The federal government presented the draft decree that seeks
to guarantee safe digital environments for children and adolescents, under
which **digital platforms will be obligated to take down content that incites
violence** with hate speech and violent extremism; sexual abuse, exploitation
or violence; suicide, deliberate self-harm and eating disorders, among other
aspects.

President Claudia Sheinbaum asserted that the platforms will be obligated to
take down this content and report to the Secretariat of Security and Citizen
Protection and the National Guard when they identify this type of violent
content. However, she specified that **for now there is no intention to
incorporate sanctions** for companies that fail to comply with these
obligations because no one can be against not disseminating sexual abuse or
violent content.

Sheinbaum mentioned that this decree will be published next week to allow a
few days to talk with the representatives of the companies to discuss the
scope of this decree. Nevertheless, she emphasized that this is a mandatory
decree because we cannot allow platforms not to be safe spaces for children
and adolescents.

However, the president considered it very important that this decree take
effect as soon as possible, specifying that it was **a commitment she made to
society after the attack at a school in Coahuila**.

She noted that there have been meetings with experts and members of the
security cabinet as well as authorities from the Secretariat of Public
Education and the Secretariat of Health to fine-tune this decree.

In this regard, the head of the Digital Transformation Agency, José Antonio
Peña Merino, said that the platforms already have many security mechanisms in
force to remove violent or sexual abuse content. It is a matter of fine-tuning
these types of policies and speeding up reporting to the security authorities.

The president explained that the decree would be published between Tuesday and
Wednesday and that a working group will be formed to analyze whether it is
necessary to go further and draft legal reforms.
